pharm: Blocks cholinergic stimulation of the iris sphincter and ciliary muscles, producing pupil dilation (mydriasis) and, at higher strength, paralysis of accommodation (cycloplegia)
quick: Refraction: 1-2 drops of 1%, repeat in 5 min; fundus exam: 1-2 drops of 0.5%, 15-20 min before
Category C; animal studies not done - use only if clearly needed
Not known if excreted in milk; use with caution
Intraocular pressure (transient rise); CNS/behavioral effects in children
summary: Tropicamide is a short-acting topical ophthalmic anticholinergic used to produce mydriasis and cycloplegia for diagnostic procedures such as refraction and fundus examination. The 1% solution dilates the pupil and paralyzes accommodation, while the 0.5% solution gives mydriasis with only slight cycloplegia. It acts within 15-30 minutes and effects typically resolve in 4-8 hours (occasionally up to 24 hours).
indications: Mydriasis for diagnostic procedures (e.g. fundus examination)

dosage.d: 1 or 2 drops of 1% solution in the eye(s), repeated in 5 minutes
dosage.t: If patient not seen within 20-30 min, an additional drop may be instilled to prolong mydriasis
dosage.n: Heavily pigmented irides may require higher strength or more doses

dosage.d: 1 or 2 drops of 0.5% solution 15 to 20 minutes before examination
dosage.n: 0.5% gives mydriasis with only slight cycloplegia

admin: For topical ophthalmic use only - not for injection
Instill drops into the conjunctival sac; do not touch the dropper tip to any surface
Compress the lacrimal sac with digital pressure for 2-3 minutes after instillation to reduce systemic absorption
Patients should protect eyes from bright light and avoid driving/hazardous activities while pupils are dilated
moa: This anticholinergic (antimuscarinic) preparation blocks the responses of the sphincter muscle of the iris and the ciliary muscle to cholinergic stimulation, dilating the pupil (mydriasis); the stronger (1%) preparation also paralyzes accommodation (cycloplegia). It acts in 15-30 minutes, with a duration of activity of approximately 3-8 hours. Heavily pigmented irides may require more doses than lightly pigmented irides.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to any component of the preparation
relative: Narrow anterior chamber angle / risk of angle-closure glaucoma (may precipitate an attack)
Pediatric patients (risk of CNS disturbances and behavioral effects)
monitor: CNS / behavioral effects, particularly in infants and children

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with tropicamide, and it is not known whether tropicamide can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity when given to a pregnant woman. It should be given to a pregnant woman only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether tropicamide is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in milk, caution should be exercised when tropicamide is administered to a nursing woman.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described; systemic absorption from topical ophthalmic use is minimal, especially with nasolacrimal occlusion.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described for topical ophthalmic use.

moderate: Carbachol, pilocarpine, or ophthalmic cholinesterase inhibitors - tropicamide may interfere with their antihypertensive (miotic/IOP-lowering) action
interactions.diagnostics: Pupil dilation interferes with assessment of the pupillary light reflex during the duration of action

serious: Increased intraocular pressure / precipitation of angle-closure glaucoma
CNS disturbances and behavioral disturbances (especially children)
emergency: Psychotic reactions and behavioral disturbances in children
Vasomotor or cardio-respiratory collapse in children (with anticholinergic drugs)

monitoring: Intraocular pressure (transient elevation, risk of angle closure)
CNS and behavioral status, particularly in infants and children
Visual recovery (mydriasis reverses in 4-8 hours, up to 24 hours)
Anterior chamber angle assessment before use in susceptible patients
counsel: Your vision will be blurred and your eyes sensitive to light for several hours, sometimes up to a day
Do not drive or do hazardous activities until your vision returns to normal; wear sunglasses in bright light
Briefly press the inner corner of your eye after the drops to reduce body-wide absorption
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface; remove contact lenses first
For children: do not let the medicine get into the child's mouth and wash hands after use; seek help for unusual drowsiness, confusion, or behavior changes
pk: Maximal mydriasis approximately 20-40 minutes after instillation
Not characterized for topical ophthalmic use (rapidly redistributed/metabolized)
Approximately 3-8 hours; complete recovery in some individuals may take up to 24 hours
Store at 8 to 27 C (46 to 80 F); do not refrigerate or store at high temperatures; keep container tightly closed
pearls: Short-acting anticholinergic mydriatic/cycloplegic of choice for routine diagnostic dilation - faster offset than atropine or cyclopentolate
1% gives mydriasis plus cycloplegia (refraction); 0.5% gives mydriasis with only slight cycloplegia (fundoscopy)
Can precipitate acute angle-closure glaucoma in eyes with narrow angles - assess the anterior chamber first
Heavily pigmented irides bind drug and may need higher strength or additional drops
Nasolacrimal occlusion after instillation reduces systemic anticholinergic absorption, important in children and the elderly
missed: Not applicable - tropicamide is administered as a single diagnostic dose by or under the direction of a clinician, not on a self-administered repeating schedule.
overdose: Systemic anticholinergic toxicity from excessive ocular dosing or accidental ingestion may produce dry mouth, flushing, tachycardia, fever, blurred vision, urinary retention, CNS disturbances (restlessness, hallucinations, behavioral changes), and in children psychotic reactions or vasomotor/cardio-respiratory collapse. Treatment is supportive; severe systemic antimuscarinic toxicity may be managed with physostigmine and supportive measures. Minimize systemic absorption with nasolacrimal occlusion.
